hook_text: Draw one line on a rainfall map of South Africa, and you can explain where people lived for a thousand years.
clip_script: Rain in South Africa falls mostly in the east, and mostly in summer. Draw a line where the rain reaches about five hundred millimetres a year. East of it, sorghum and millet, African grains that love summer storms, can grow. So that's where African farmers settled, from about two thousand years ago: villages, iron hoes, granaries full of grain, and cattle kraals at the centre of every homestead. West of the line, too dry for crops, San hunters and Khoikhoi herders lived. Geography shaped history.
visual_style: A rainfall map of South Africa shades from dark blue in the east to pale yellow in the west; a line is drawn down the middle; sorghum heads, a kraal and huts appear on the east side, a herder and sheep on the west.
mood: Clear and engaging, like a map reveal.
pacing: One idea at a time, building to the final line.
